version.changelog: README productization upgrade with proof and outcome framing

llm.summary: The skill's description and bundled data/scripts match its UI-design purpose, but a prompt-injection signal in SKILL.md plus bundled executable Python scripts (with no explicit install or declared credentials) make it worth auditing before running.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, the large local data/CSV knowledge base, and the listed scripts (search, core, design_system, style_signature) are coherent: they reasonably support generating design systems and mapping them to code. The large font and style CSVs and references align with the stated goal.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent to run local Python scripts (e.g. python3 skills/ui-craft-pro/scripts/search.py ...) which is expected for this skill, but the pre-scan flagged a 'system-prompt-override' pattern inside SKILL.md (prompt-injection). That could attempt to alter agent/system behavior at runtime. The instructions do not declare reading unrelated system files or env vars, but the scripts (not fully shown) are executable and could access environment, network, or disk beyond the skill's data folder.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no install spec (lowest install risk), and all data and Python scripts are bundled. However, SKILL.md explicitly tells the agent to execute those bundled scripts; executing supplied code is higher risk than a pure instruction-only skill because the code can perform arbitrary actions (including network I/O). The only shown script excerpt (data/_sync_all.py) appears to operate on local CSVs and is benign, but the larger scripts were not shown in full in the manifest and should be inspected before execution.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials, which fits a local design tool. That said, bundled Python scripts could still read environment variables or secrets at runtime; lack of declared env vars means any such access would be an undisclosed risk. Confirm scripts do not attempt to read or exfiltrate secrets/environment variables.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Flags show always:false and normal agent invocation. The skill does not request persistent inclusion or elevated platform privileges. No config paths or system-level modifications are declared in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is plausible for UI work: it bundles a local design knowledge base and scripts to search and generate design systems. However, before running anything, do the following: 1) Manually inspect the full contents of the bundled Python scripts (scripts/*.py) for any network calls (requests, urllib, socket), subprocess execution, or references to os.environ, open(..., 'w'), or unexpected file paths. 2) Check SKILL.md for any sections that try to alter system prompts or give broad agent instructions (the pre-scan flagged this). 3) If you cannot audit the code, run it in a restricted sandbox or ephemeral environment without access to credentials or sensitive files. 4) If you will run it within an agent that has access to secrets, ensure the scripts do not read environment variables or write outbound network connections. If you want, share the full contents of scripts/core.py and scripts/design_system.py and I can flag any suspicious code patterns specifically.
llm.findings: [system-prompt-override] unexpected: The prompt-injection detector found a 'system-prompt-override' pattern inside SKILL.md. A UI design skill should not need to modify the agent's system prompt or internal instructions. This could be an attempt to change agent behavior and should be manually inspected.
